model.author: Bio3D Project
model.modifications: Procedural 3D complete bisexual flower model exported as GLB.

short.en: Brightly coloured leaf-like parts that attract bees, butterflies, and birds for pollination.

detail.en: Collectively form the corolla (second floral whorl). Bright colours and scents attract biotic pollinators; they also shield inner reproductive whorls in the bud.

short.en: Green leaf-like parts under the petals that protect the flower while it is still a bud.

detail.en: Outermost floral whorl (calyx). Usually green and photosynthetic, enclosing and protecting the unopened flower bud.

short.en: The male part of the flower made of a stalk (filament) and a pollen-making head (anther).

detail.en: Collectively form the androecium. Consists of a slender filament supporting a bilobed anther that produces pollen grains (male gametophytes). In NEET mode, filament and anther are shown separately.

short.en: The central female part with a sticky top (stigma), tube (style), and swollen base (ovary).

detail.en: Collectively form the gynoecium. Consists of stigma (receives pollen), style (conducts pollen tube), and ovary (contains ovules). After fertilisation, the ovary becomes the fruit.

short.en: Tiny egg-holding structures inside the ovary that turn into seeds after fertilisation.

detail.en: Megasporangia attached to the placenta inside the ovary. Each ovule contains the embryo sac (female gametophyte) with the egg cell and central cell; develops into a seed post-fertilisation.

short.en: The swollen top of the flower stalk that holds all the parts of the flower together.

detail.en: Condensed floral axis (thalamus/torus) bearing the four floral whorls (calyx, corolla, androecium, gynoecium) at closely spaced nodes.

short.en: The green stem that supports the flower and connects it to the plant branch.

detail.en: Stalk of an individual flower containing vascular bundles that supply water, minerals, and sugars to developing floral organs and fruits.

short.en: Pollen-producing sac at the tip of the stamen.

detail.en: Typically bilobed and dithecous (four microsporangia). Inside, pollen mother cells undergo meiosis to form haploid microspores (pollen grains), nourished by the tapetum.

short.en: Slender stalk holding the anther up to release pollen.

detail.en: Long, slender sterile stalk whose proximal end attaches to the thalamus or petal (epipetalous) and whose distal end supports the anther.

short.en: Sticky landing platform at the top of the pistil that catches pollen.

detail.en: Receptive tip of the carpel. Recognises compatible pollen grains via chemical pollen-pistil interaction and stimulates pollen germination.

short.en: Slender neck connecting the stigma down to the ovary.

detail.en: Elongated hollow or solid tissue column beneath the stigma through which the pollen tube grows downward toward the ovules.

short.en: Enlarged hollow base of the pistil enclosing the ovules; ripens into the fruit.

detail.en: Basal swollen region of the pistil housing one or more locules (ovarian cavities) with ovules attached to the placenta. Post-fertilisation, the ovary wall becomes the pericarp (fruit).

short.en: Sweet sugar-secreting glands at the flower base that reward insect pollinators.

detail.en: Secretory glands located near the petal/receptacle base producing sugary nectar as a reward to ensure cross-pollination (entomophily / ornithophily).

question.en: Tap the brightly coloured parts that attract insects to the flower.

explanation.en: Petals (the corolla) use bright colours and pleasant scents to guide bees and butterflies to the flower.

question.en: Which part of a flower grows into seeds after fertilisation?

explanation.en: Ovules inside the ovary develop into seeds, while the surrounding ovary ripens into the fruit.

question.en: Tap the green outer flaps that protect the flower while it is a bud.

explanation.en: Sepals form the calyx around the outside of the flower bud to keep it safe before blooming.

question.en: Tap the bilobed pollen-producing structure where microsporogenesis occurs.

explanation.en: The anther contains microsporangia where pollen mother cells divide by meiosis to form pollen grains.

question.en: Which tissue inside a dithecous anther nourishes the developing pollen grains?

explanation.en: The tapetum is the innermost layer of the microsporangium wall; its dense, multinucleate cells nourish developing pollen grains.
